name: Limit Break Payment Processor V2 forwarded-calldata offset sender spoof
summary: Payment Processor V2 copies a forwarded call's trade data from the caller-supplied ABI offset but sizes the copy as if the offset were canonical. Sending offset 0 through a permissionless trusted forwarder shifts the copy, drops the forwarder-appended real sender and lets attacker bytes become the ERC-2771 sender, so the attacker could act as any wallet that had approved Payment Processor: accepting its own zero-price offers for victims' NFTs and making victims buy worthless listings with approved WETH and stablecoins.
notes: Immutable PaymentProcessor V2 runtime contains the fixed 68-byte offset assumption in delegateCallReplaceDomainSeparator; permissionless forwarder registration and collection settings add no causal configuration.

Exact victim ERC-20 debits from spoofed buy-listing calls on Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum (sibling V2 deployments) and ApeChain (PP V3, identical modifier, same actors and forwarder 0xb48d6af77c5e3b99876ea71b38e9c814ba5b1c8e), totalling $1,665,921.59 at DefiLlama prices of each asset's first drain. The stolen NFTs (at least 84612 ERC721 items and 77264 ERC1155 units from 12769 Ethereum wallets, plus the other-chain events counted in source-3) are unvalued, so this amount is a lower bound; SlowMist reports about $2.8M. Scan ends: Ethereum block 26078818, Base 51922870, Polygon 94620091, Arbitrum 509846310, BNB 124606568, OP 157518303, ApeChain 50588304; later drains are not included.
Stolen NFTs are counted but not valued; loss.usd covers only exactly measured ERC-20 victim debits and is a lower bound.
Ethereum NFT events with EIP-7702 or contract takers (22894 ERC721, 3177 ERC1155) and other-chain NFT events are classified by taker != transaction sender, not individually traced.
The campaign was still active at the scan end blocks listed in loss.notes; later drains are excluded.
